components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 老师今天布置了很多作业。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jīntiān bùzhì le hěn duō zuòyè.
example.english: The teacher assigned a lot of homework today.
example.fact: 作业 covers both a student's "homework" and a more general "task, operation" in technical or industrial contexts (施工作业 "construction work") — the same word spans a school desk and a construction site, unified by 业's core sense of an undertaking or occupation.

examples.hanzi: 我做完作业了，可以出去玩吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò wán zuòyè le, kěyǐ chūqù wán ma?
examples.english: I've finished my homework; may I go out to play?

examples.hanzi: 老师检查了我们的作业。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiǎnchá le wǒmen de zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher checked our homework.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 这是一家非常高级的餐厅。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì jiā fēicháng gāojí de cāntīng.
example.english: This is a very high-end restaurant.
example.fact: 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread (its 纟 radical still carries that "thread" sense) — the image of individual threads ranked by grade extended naturally to today's meaning "level, grade, rank," the same logic behind words like 年级 ("grade level in school").

examples.hanzi: 这个手机的功能很高级。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī de gōngnéng hěn gāojí.
examples.english: This phone has very advanced features.

examples.hanzi: 他是公司的高级经理。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōngsī de gāojí jīnglǐ.
examples.english: He is a senior manager at the company.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放; 敬 is respectful behaviour, as in 尊敬.
苟 (gǒu) — sound clue is weak — 敬 is jìng, but 敬 sounds out 警 jǐng.

example.hanzi: 我们都很尊敬老师。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu hěn zūnjìng lǎoshī.
example.english: We all respect our teacher.
example.fact: 敬 means to respect and also to offer politely: 敬酒 is to toast someone at a banquet and show respect. 敬礼 is a salute, 恭敬 is respectful, and 敬酒不吃吃罚酒 is the idiom for refusing a polite offer.

examples.hanzi: 我想敬你一杯,谢谢你的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jìng nǐ yì bēi, xièxie nǐ de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I'd like to toast you to thank you for your help.

examples.hanzi: 新郎新娘向客人敬酒。
examples.pinyin: Xīnláng xīnniáng xiàng kèrén jìngjiǔ.
examples.english: The bride and groom offer toasts to the guests.

components.note: 丬 (bed/couch, left side) — the left strip, a bed seen sideways. Dictionary story: going to bed at night, the 'future' that is sure to come; read as a memory aid.
夕 (evening) — upper part of the right side, as in 外 and 多; with 寸 (hand/inch) it frames 将 meaning 'about to / will'.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 他将来想当一名医生。
example.pinyin: Tā jiānglái xiǎng dāng yì míng yīshēng.
example.english: In the future, he wants to become a doctor.
example.fact: 将来 and its near-synonym 未来 both mean "the future," but 将来 leans toward a nearer future tied to someone's own plans, while 未来 reads as more general or distant — a nuance easy to miss since English "future" covers both without distinction.

examples.hanzi: 将来的世界会是什么样子？
examples.pinyin: Jiānglái de shìjiè huì shì shénme yàngzi?
examples.english: What will the world look like in the future?

examples.hanzi: 你将来想做什么工作？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiānglái xiǎng zuò shénme gōngzuò?
examples.english: What kind of job do you want to do in the future?

components.note: 而 (and, beard) — the left part and radical; originally a beard. Memory aid: stroking a beard while waiting, a patient person, as in 耐心.
寸 (inch/hand) — the right part, as in 对 and 村; here it means a hand. In 耐 it suggests a hand with patience to measure; Memory aid only.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 老师对学生一直很有耐心。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì xuésheng yìzhí hěn yǒu nàixīn.
example.english: The teacher has always been very patient with the students.
example.fact: 耐心 pairs 耐 ("to endure, to withstand," as in 耐用 "durable") with 心 ("heart, mind") — literally "an enduring heart" — the same 耐 that describes a durable material describes a durable temperament when applied to patience.

examples.hanzi: 学习外语需要很大的耐心。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí wàiyǔ xūyào hěn dà de nàixīn.
examples.english: Learning a foreign language takes a lot of patience.

examples.hanzi: 请耐心等一下，医生马上就来。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nàixīn děng yíxià, yīshēng mǎshàng jiù lái.
examples.english: Please wait patiently; the doctor will be here shortly.

meanings: Europe (abbr. for 歐羅巴洲|欧罗巴洲[Ou1 luo2 ba1 Zhou1])

components.note: 区 (qū) — near sound — 欧 is ōu; 区 also sounds out 殴 ōu and 呕 ǒu.
欠 (open mouth) — 欠 shows an open mouth, as in 吹, 歌, 欢; 欧 is mostly seen in 欧洲 Europe.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洲 is land surrounded by water.
州 (zhōu) — same sound — 洲 is zhōu, like 州; continents like 亚洲 are 洲.

example.hanzi: 他计划暑假去欧洲旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā jìhuà shǔjià qù Ōuzhōu lǚxíng.
example.english: He's planning to travel to Europe during summer vacation.
example.fact: 洲 is the standard suffix for continents in Chinese — 亚洲 (Asia), 非洲 (Africa), and 美洲 (the Americas) all end the same way — while 欧 itself is purely a phonetic syllable borrowed to represent the "Eu-" sound of "Europe," carrying no meaning of its own.

examples.hanzi: 欧洲有很多历史悠久的城市。
examples.pinyin: Ōuzhōu yǒu hěn duō lìshǐ yōujiǔ de chéngshì.
examples.english: Europe has many cities with a long history.

examples.hanzi: 从欧洲飞到中国要十多个小时。
examples.pinyin: Cóng Ōuzhōu fēi dào Zhōngguó yào shí duō ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: It takes more than ten hours to fly from Europe to China.

components.note: 風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: a steep place, a risky pass.
佥 (qiān) is a loose sound clue for xiǎn; 佥 also in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 验 yàn.

example.hanzi: 投资股票总是有一定的风险。
example.pinyin: Tóuzī gǔpiào zǒngshì yǒu yídìng de fēngxiǎn.
example.english: Investing in stocks always carries a certain amount of risk.
example.fact: 险 alone already means "danger, precipitous" (its 阝 radical points to the steep, treacherous terrain in its original sense) — adding 风 ("wind") on top gives learners a handy image of risk as an unpredictable danger that can shift like the weather, though this pairing is best treated as a descriptive gloss rather than a documented historical origin.

examples.hanzi: 做生意总是有风险的。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shēngyi zǒngshì yǒu fēngxiǎn de.
examples.english: Doing business always involves risk.

examples.hanzi: 这种药的风险很小，你不用担心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào de fēngxiǎn hěn xiǎo, nǐ búyòng dānxīn.
examples.english: The risk of this medicine is very low, so don't worry.

meanings: (Internet slang) first reply to a forum post

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; sand grains are tiny bits washed by water.
少 (shǎo) — near sound — 沙 is shā; 少 also sounds out 炒 chǎo and 纱 shā.
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.hanzi: 他懒懒地躺在沙发上看电视。
example.pinyin: Tā lǎnlǎn de tǎng zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì.
example.english: He lazily lay on the sofa watching TV.
example.fact: 沙发 is a phonetic loanword for "sofa," with 发 borrowed purely for its fā sound and no connection to its usual meanings ("hair" or "to send out") — Chinese Internet slang later reused the same two characters for an unrelated joke, "grabbing the sofa" (占沙发), meaning to post the very first reply in an online discussion thread.

examples.hanzi: 我们家新买了一个大沙发。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā xīn mǎi le yí ge dà shāfā.
examples.english: We just bought a big new sofa for our home.

examples.hanzi: 朋友来我家时，可以睡在沙发上。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou lái wǒ jiā shí, kěyǐ shuì zài shāfā shang.
examples.english: When friends visit, they can sleep on the sofa.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — blocking with the hand; also in 推 push, 打 hit.
当 (dāng) gives the sound, with a different tone; 档 dàng shares it.

example.hanzi: 别挡住我的路。
example.pinyin: Bié dǎngzhù wǒ de lù.
example.english: Don't block my way.
example.fact: 挡 is to block or shield: 挡住 (block), 阻挡 (obstruct), 挡风 (shelter from wind). On a car, 挡 is also a gear: 换挡 (shift gears), 一挡 (first gear).

examples.hanzi: 前面的车挡住了我的视线。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn de chē dǎng zhù le wǒ de shìxiàn.
examples.english: The car ahead blocked my view.

examples.hanzi: 出门带把伞挡雨吧。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén dài bǎ sǎn dǎng yǔ ba.
examples.english: Take an umbrella to keep the rain off.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐, 妒; 奸 is old usage for crafty or illicit behaviour.
干 (gān) — near sound — 奸 is jiān; 干 also sounds out 肝 gān and 杆 gān.

example.hanzi: 那个案件的被告被指控强奸。
example.pinyin: Nàge ànjiàn de bèigào bèi zhǐkòng qiángjiān.
example.english: The defendant in that case was accused of rape.
example.fact: 强 here keeps its core sense of "by force, forcibly" (as in 强迫 "to force, to coerce") rather than its more common meaning "strong" — legal Chinese consistently uses 强奸 as the formal, neutral term in statutes and court documents rather than a euphemism.

examples.hanzi: 强奸是严重的犯罪，法律会严厉惩罚。
examples.pinyin: Qiángjiān shì yánzhòng de fànzuì, fǎlǜ huì yánlì chéngfá.
examples.english: Rape is a serious crime, and the law punishes it severely.

examples.hanzi: 警方正在调查一起强奸案。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá yì qǐ qiángjiān àn.
examples.english: The police are investigating a rape case.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 他没有考虑后果就做了决定。
example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu kǎolǜ hòuguǒ jiù zuò le juédìng.
example.english: He made the decision without considering the consequences.
example.fact: 果 keeps its literal sense of "fruit" even here — 后果 pictures consequences as the "fruit that comes after" an action, almost always used for a negative or undesirable outcome rather than a neutral or positive one.

examples.hanzi: 你应该想一想这样做的后果。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi xiǎng yi xiǎng zhèyàng zuò de hòuguǒ.
examples.english: You should think about the consequences of doing this.

examples.hanzi: 不努力的后果是考试不及格。
examples.pinyin: Bù nǔlì de hòuguǒ shì kǎoshì bù jígé.
examples.english: The result of not working hard is failing the exam.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 is grass and plants, as in 草, 花, 菜; 荒 is land overgrown with weeds, wasteland.
亡 (wáng) — loose hint — 荒 is huāng; 亡 also sounds out 慌 huāng, 谎 huǎng and 忙 máng.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话; 谬 is speech that is wrong or absurd.
翏 (liù) — near sound — 谬 is miù; 翏 also sounds out 缪 miù.

example.hanzi: 这个理由听起来非常荒谬。
example.pinyin: Zhège lǐyóu tīng qǐlai fēicháng huāngmiù.
example.english: This reason sounds extremely absurd.
example.fact: 荒 contributes a sense of "wild, overgrown, uncultivated" (as in 荒地 "wasteland") and 谬 means "mistaken, erroneous" — 荒谬 combines them into an idea one step past a simple mistake: a claim so far off from reason that it reads as wildly, almost comically wrong.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事太荒谬了，没人会相信。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi tài huāngmiù le, méi rén huì xiāngxìn.
examples.english: This story is too ridiculous; nobody would believe it.

examples.hanzi: 他提出了一个荒谬的要求。
examples.pinyin: Tā tíchū le yí ge huāngmiù de yāoqiú.
examples.english: He made an absurd request.

components.note: 人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子从小就很有个性。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi cóngxiǎo jiù hěn yǒu gèxìng.
example.english: This child has had a lot of personality since childhood.
example.fact: 个性 specifically highlights the distinctive traits that set one person apart from others — its close relative 性格 covers someone's overall temperament more broadly, so 有个性 ("to have personality") praises someone's distinctiveness in a way 性格 alone doesn't quite capture.

examples.hanzi: 每个人的个性都不一样。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén de gèxìng dōu bù yíyàng.
examples.english: Everyone has a different personality.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服很有个性，我很喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn yǒu gèxìng, wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
examples.english: This piece of clothing has real character, and I like it a lot.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 移 first meant grain swaying, then shifting and moving.
多 (duō) — the original sound clue — today 移 yí is only loosely related to 多 duō.

example.hanzi: 请把桌子往左移一点。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi wǎng zuǒ yí yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please move the table a little to the left.
example.fact: 移 means to shift something, and is the root of 移动 (to move; also 'mobile'), 移民 (to immigrate) and 转移 (to transfer). The tale 愚公移山 tells of a man who tried to move mountains with perseverance.

examples.hanzi: 他把椅子移到窗边。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yǐzi yí dào chuāng biān.
examples.english: He moved the chair to the window.

examples.hanzi: 我们明年要移民加拿大。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngnián yào yímín Jiānádà.
examples.english: We're going to emigrate to Canada next year.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pushing aside by hand; also in 推 push, 拉 pull.
发 (fā) is only a loose clue; it also sounds out 泼 pō.

example.hanzi: 请拨这个电话号码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bō zhège diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.english: Please dial this phone number.
example.fact: 拨 means to push aside or flick, and so to dial: 拨号 (dial), 拨打电话 (make a call). It also means to allocate (拨款, release funds), and counts batches of people as 一拨人.

examples.hanzi: 你拨一下他的号码。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bō yíxià tā de hàomǎ.
examples.english: Dial his number.

examples.hanzi: 他拨开人群走了过去。
examples.pinyin: Tā bō kāi rénqún zǒu le guòqù.
examples.english: He pushed through the crowd.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a person kneeling at food 皀, about to eat: right at hand, immediately; compare 既, who has already eaten.

example.hanzi: 他一听到消息,即刻出发了。
example.pinyin: Tā yì tīngdào xiāoxi, jíkè chūfā le.
example.english: As soon as he heard the news, he set off at once.
example.fact: 即 is formal 'immediately/namely': 即将 (about to), 即使 (even if), 立即 (immediately). It is a counterpart to 既, which shows the same person turning away from the food.

examples.hanzi: 即使下雨,我们也要去。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ xià yǔ, wǒmen yě yào qù.
examples.english: Even if it rains, we're going.

examples.hanzi: 这个手机即将上市。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī jíjiāng shàngshì.
examples.english: This phone is about to go on sale.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 你最好现在就出发,不然会迟到。
example.pinyin: Nǐ zuìhǎo xiànzài jiù chūfā, bùrán huì chídào.
example.english: You'd better leave right now, or you'll be late.
example.fact: Beyond its plain sense "best," 最好 doubles as a softened suggestion meaning "had better," similar to how English "best" shows up in "you'd best leave now" — in this second use it's less a superlative and more a gentle warning about what happens if the advice isn't followed.

examples.hanzi: 天气不好，你最好别出门。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì bù hǎo, nǐ zuìhǎo bié chū mén.
examples.english: The weather is bad, so you'd better not go out.

examples.hanzi: 这是我吃过的最好的蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ chī guo de zuì hǎo de dàngāo.
examples.english: This is the best cake I've ever eaten.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这项工作男性和女性都可以申请。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng gōngzuò nánxìng hé nǚxìng dōu kěyǐ shēnqǐng.
example.english: Both men and women can apply for this job.
example.fact: 男性 is the clinical, formal term for biological sex used on official forms and in medical or demographic contexts — everyday speech almost always prefers the plainer 男人 ("man") instead, the same formal/informal split seen between 女性 and 女人.

examples.hanzi: 男性和女性的平均寿命不同。
examples.pinyin: Nánxìng hé nǚxìng de píngjūn shòumìng bù tóng.
examples.english: The average life expectancy differs between men and women.

examples.hanzi: 这家健身房的会员大部分是男性。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiànshēnfáng de huìyuán dà bùfen shì nánxìng.
examples.english: Most members of this gym are men.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢收集邮票。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan shōují yóupiào.
example.english: He has liked collecting stamps since childhood.
example.fact: 集 pictures a bird (隹) perched in a tree (木) — originally suggesting birds flocking together — and that image of many separate things gathering into one place carries directly into modern words like 收集 ("to collect"), 集市 ("market"), and even 集 for a TV episode (第一集 "episode one").

examples.hanzi: 我们正在收集大家的意见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhèngzài shōují dàjiā de yìjiàn.
examples.english: We are collecting everyone's opinions.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢收集漂亮的石头。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan shōují piàoliang de shítou.
examples.english: She likes collecting pretty stones.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他们交往三年后决定结婚。
example.pinyin: Tāmen jiāowǎng sān nián hòu juédìng jiéhūn.
example.english: After dating for three years, they decided to get married.
example.fact: 交往 spans a spectrum from plain "social contact" to specifically "romantic dating," and context alone decides which sense applies — 和他交往 could mean simply "to associate with him" or "to date him," a genuine ambiguity that doesn't exist in English's separate words.

examples.hanzi: 他和女朋友交往两年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé nǚ péngyou jiāowǎng liǎng nián le.
examples.english: He has been dating his girlfriend for two years.

examples.hanzi: 和不同的人交往能让你学到很多。
examples.pinyin: Hé bù tóng de rén jiāowǎng néng ràng nǐ xué dào hěn duō.
examples.english: Associating with different people lets you learn a lot.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 你是哪国人?
example.pinyin: Nǐ shì nǎ guó rén?
example.english: What country are you from?
example.fact: 国 appears in the names of countries: 中国, 美国 (literally 'beautiful country'), 英国, 法国. 中国 originally meant 'central state'. 国家 means country or nation, and 外国 means foreign country.

examples.hanzi: 我想去很多国家旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù hěn duō guójiā lǚxíng.
examples.english: I want to travel to many countries.

examples.hanzi: 他是在国外长大的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zài guówài zhǎngdà de.
examples.english: He grew up abroad.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
尸 (body/cover) — the top-left part, as in 局 and 层. Origin in 尉 is unclear; it is only a visible part.
寸 (inch/hand) — the right part and radical, as in 对 and 村. Memory aid: an officer with a hand on the order, as in 上尉 captain.

example.hanzi: 他二十五岁就当上了中尉。
example.pinyin: Tā èrshíwǔ suì jiù dāng shàng le zhōngwèi.
example.english: He became a lieutenant at the age of twenty-five.
example.fact: Chinese military ranks stack 中 ("middle") between 少 ("junior") and 上 ("senior") across a whole parallel rank system — 少尉/中尉/上尉 (second lieutenant/lieutenant/captain) mirrors 少校/中校/上校 (major/lieutenant colonel/colonel) one tier up, so learning this 少-中-上 pattern once unlocks several rank names at once.

examples.hanzi: 中尉带领士兵们回到了基地。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngwèi dàilǐng shìbīngmen huí dào le jīdì.
examples.english: The lieutenant led the soldiers back to the base.

examples.hanzi: 这位中尉已经服役五年了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhōngwèi yǐjīng fúyì wǔ nián le.
examples.english: This lieutenant has served for five years.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 她通过努力取得了很好的成绩。
example.pinyin: Tā tōngguò nǔlì qǔdé le hěn hǎo de chéngjì.
example.english: Through hard work, she achieved very good grades.
example.fact: 取得 doubles up two independent "to obtain" verbs — 取 (traditionally linked to taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill in ancient battle) and 得 (a hand reaching for a valuable shell) — into one formal verb reserved for achievements or results (取得成功, 取得学位), rarely used for grabbing a simple physical object.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中取得了第一名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng qǔdé le dì-yī míng.
examples.english: He won first place in the competition.

examples.hanzi: 你需要取得老师的同意才能进去。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xūyào qǔdé lǎoshī de tóngyì cái néng jìnqù.
examples.english: You need to obtain the teacher's permission to go in.

components.note: 上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 卡尔是我们班唯一的德国学生。
example.pinyin: Kǎ'ěr shì wǒmen bān wéiyī de Déguó xuésheng.
example.english: Karl is the only German student in our class.
example.fact: 卡尔 is a phonetic transliteration of the Western name "Karl/Carl" with no meaning intended — the same 卡 syllable, chosen purely for its kǎ sound, also shows up transliterating "card" (卡片, informally just 卡) and dozens of other loanwords, since it carries no strong native meaning of its own to get in the way.

examples.hanzi: 卡尔每天坐地铁去上班。
examples.pinyin: Kǎ'ěr měi tiān zuò dìtiě qù shàngbān.
examples.english: Karl takes the subway to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天遇到了卡尔，他问你好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān yùdào le Kǎ'ěr, tā wèn nǐ hǎo.
examples.english: I ran into Karl yesterday, and he says hello.

components.note: 至 (zhì) — same sound — 致 is zhì, like 至 (to arrive); 致 is to cause to arrive, then to bring about.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action performed, as in 教, 放, 收.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.hanzi: 那次车祸对他造成了致命的伤害。
example.pinyin: Nà cì chēhuò duì tā zàochéng le zhìmìng de shānghài.
example.english: That car accident caused him a fatal injury.
example.fact: 致 carries a sense of "to cause, to bring about" (as in 致使 "to cause, to result in") — 致命 literally means "to bring about death" — and that same formal 致 also opens the salutation of a letter (致 + recipient, "To So-and-so"), a very different register from the deadly compound it forms here.

examples.hanzi: 这种蛇的毒是致命的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shé de dú shì zhìmìng de.
examples.english: This snake's venom is deadly.

examples.hanzi: 一个小错误也可能带来致命的后果。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge xiǎo cuòwù yě kěnéng dàilái zhìmìng de hòuguǒ.
examples.english: Even a small mistake can have fatal consequences.

components.note: 乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.
日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 中国成功发射了一颗新卫星。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó chénggōng fāshè le yì kē xīn wèixīng.
example.english: China successfully launched a new satellite.
example.fact: 卫 carries the sense "to guard, to defend" (as in 保卫 "to defend, to protect") — 卫星 literally means "guard star," picturing a satellite as a small body that stands watch in orbit around its larger companion, whether that's a planet's moon or a man-made craft circling Earth.

examples.hanzi: 月亮是地球唯一的天然卫星。
examples.pinyin: Yuèliang shì dìqiú wéiyī de tiānrán wèixīng.
examples.english: The moon is Earth's only natural satellite.

examples.hanzi: 很多手机导航都要依靠卫星。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō shǒujī dǎoháng dōu yào yīkào wèixīng.
examples.english: Many phone navigation systems rely on satellites.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.

example.hanzi: 这个故事吸引了很多人。
example.pinyin: Zhège gùshi xīyǐn le hěn duō rén.
example.english: This story attracted many people.
example.fact: 引 started as drawing a bow and extends to attracting and quoting: 吸引 (attract), 引起 (cause), 引用 (quote), 引导 (guide). 引号 are quotation marks, and 引擎 is a transliteration of 'engine'.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的广告引起了大家的注意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de guǎnggào yǐnqǐ le dàjiā de zhùyì.
examples.english: This shop's ad caught everyone's attention.

examples.hanzi: 我引他们去会议室。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐn tāmen qù huìyìshì.
examples.english: I'll lead them to the meeting room.

components.note: 月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 父母对他的期望很高。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ duì tā de qīwàng hěn gāo.
example.english: His parents have high expectations of him.
example.fact: 望 pictures a person standing tall, straining to gaze into the distance at the moon — the same character that means "to look toward" extends naturally to "hope, to expect," since both involve looking ahead toward something not yet present, a link 期望 makes explicit by pairing it with 期 ("a period of time").

examples.hanzi: 老师对我们的期望很高。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì wǒmen de qīwàng hěn gāo.
examples.english: The teacher has high expectations of us.

examples.hanzi: 我期望明年能去国外读书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qīwàng míngnián néng qù guówài dú shū.
examples.english: I hope to study abroad next year.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 嘲 is mocking speech.
朝 (cháo) — same sound — 嘲 is cháo, like 朝; 朝 also sounds out 潮 cháo.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 别人嘲笑他的口音,但他并不在意。
example.pinyin: Biérén cháoxiào tā de kǒuyīn, dàn tā bìng bú zàiyì.
example.english: Other people mocked his accent, but he didn't mind at all.
example.fact: 笑 alone is neutral or even warm ("to laugh, to smile"), but 嘲笑 flips the tone by combining it with 嘲 — a character whose 口 ("mouth") component and long-attested sense of jeering turn simple laughter into laughter aimed at someone. 笑 by itself never implies cruelty; it's 嘲 doing that work in this pair.

examples.hanzi: 同学们都嘲笑他的新帽子。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen dōu cháoxiào tā de xīn màozi.
examples.english: The classmates all laughed at his new hat.

examples.hanzi: 不要嘲笑别人的错误。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào cháoxiào biéren de cuòwù.
examples.english: Don't ridicule other people's mistakes.

components.note: 立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.
卩 (kneeling person) — a person kneeling at food 皀, about to eat: right at hand, immediately; compare 既, who has already eaten.

example.hanzi: 接到消息后,他立即赶往医院。
example.pinyin: Jiēdào xiāoxi hòu, tā lìjí gǎnwǎng yīyuàn.
example.english: After receiving the news, he immediately rushed to the hospital.
example.fact: 立即 pairs 立 ("to stand") with 即 ("right away, upon"), as if picturing something happening the instant one stands up — though 即 alone already means "immediately" (即刻), so 立 mainly reinforces the urgency. 立即 also sits at a more formal, written register than the everyday 马上, showing up constantly in official announcements and news reports.

examples.hanzi: 你一听到消息，就要立即告诉我。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yì tīngdào xiāoxi, jiù yào lìjí gàosu wǒ.
examples.english: As soon as you hear the news, tell me immediately.

examples.hanzi: 发现火灾后，请立即拨打一一九。
examples.pinyin: Fāxiàn huǒzāi hòu, qǐng lìjí bōdǎ yāo-yāo-jiǔ.
examples.english: After you discover a fire, please dial 119 immediately.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 逃; 避 is stepping aside.
辟 (bì) — same sound — 避 is bì, like 辟; 辟 also sounds out 壁 bì and 臂 bì.
⺈ (bent figure) — top part, a person; with 口 and 儿 it forms 免. Origin unclear; Memory aid: a person with a hat slipping out, 'excused'.
儿 (legs) — the bottom part and radical, a walking person, as in 先 first and 兄 older brother.

example.hanzi: 为了避免迟到,他提早出门了。
example.pinyin: Wèile bìmiǎn chídào, tā tízǎo chūmén le.
example.english: To avoid being late, he left home early.
example.fact: 避免 doubles up two overlapping "to avoid" verbs — 避 ("to evade, to dodge," sharing its 辟 phonetic with 僻 "remote, secluded") and 免 ("to escape from, to be exempt from," as in 免费 "free of charge") — reinforcing each other into the strong, general-purpose verb Chinese uses for avoiding almost any undesirable situation.

examples.hanzi: 我们要避免在高峰期出门。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bìmiǎn zài gāofēngqī chū mén.
examples.english: We should avoid going out during rush hour.

examples.hanzi: 这样做可以避免很多麻烦。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò kěyǐ bìmiǎn hěn duō máfan.
examples.english: Doing it this way can avoid a lot of trouble.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 林, 桥; here a pine tree, the original meaning.
公 (gōng) is a loose sound clue for sōng; same series 颂 sòng, 翁 wēng.

example.hanzi: 你的鞋带松了。
example.pinyin: Nǐ de xiédài sōng le.
example.english: Your shoelace has come loose.
example.fact: 松 is both 'pine' and 'loose': the 'loose' meaning was once written with a different character, 鬆, and merged into 松 when simplified. It builds 放松 and 轻松 (to relax). The pine is a symbol of endurance in 岁寒三友, the three friends of winter.

examples.hanzi: 你把绳子松一松。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ shéngzi sōng yi sōng.
examples.english: Loosen the rope a bit.

examples.hanzi: 山上有很多松树。
examples.pinyin: Shān shang yǒu hěn duō sōngshù.
examples.english: There are many pine trees on the mountain.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 供 is to supply or offer.
共 (gòng) sounds the same except tone; also in 恭 gōng and 洪 hóng.

example.hanzi: 学校为学生提供住宿。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào wèi xuésheng tígōng zhùsù.
example.english: The school provides housing for students.
example.fact: 供 is read gōng for 'supply' (提供, 供应, 供电) and gòng for 'offer, confess': 供品 (offerings), 供认 (to confess). Pay attention to the tone, since the two readings are different words.

examples.hanzi: 酒店提供免费早餐。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn tígōng miǎnfèi zǎocān.
examples.english: The hotel provides free breakfast.

examples.hanzi: 这家工厂供应全市的牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng gōngyìng quán shì de niúnǎi.
examples.english: This factory supplies milk to the whole city.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.

example.hanzi: 公司决定保留这个部门。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng bǎoliú zhège bùmén.
example.english: The company decided to keep this department.
example.fact: 保留 covers both a concrete sense ("keep, retain an object") and an abstract one ("hold back an opinion," as in 保留意见, "reservations") — a duality that traces back to 保's core sense "to protect, keep safe" plus 留's "to remain, stay behind," so retaining a stance and retaining an object share the same verb.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我保留这张收据。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎoliú zhè zhāng shōujù.
examples.english: Please help me keep this receipt.

examples.hanzi: 对这个计划，我还有一些保留意见。
examples.pinyin: Duì zhège jìhuà, wǒ hái yǒu yìxiē bǎoliú yìjiàn.
examples.english: I still have some reservations about this plan.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 按; 批 is to strike, then to comment.
比 (bǐ) is a loose hint for pī.

example.hanzi: 这批货明天到。
example.pinyin: Zhè pī huò míngtiān dào.
example.english: This batch of goods will arrive tomorrow.
example.fact: 批 works as a measure word for batches (一批货, 第一批). It also builds 批准 (to approve), 批评 (to criticize), 批发 (wholesale) and 批改 (to mark homework).

examples.hanzi: 老师在批作业。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài pī zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher is grading homework.

examples.hanzi: 第一批客人已经到了。
examples.pinyin: Dì-yī pī kèrén yǐjīng dào le.
examples.english: The first group of guests has arrived.

components.note: 各 (each) — a foot 夂 arriving at a place 口: each one coming. 各 also sounds out 路 lù, 格 gé, 客 kè and 洛 luò.
禾 (grain) — crops, as in 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 和 and 秒 second; 种 is seed or to plant.
中 (zhōng) is a close sound clue for zhǒng/zhòng.

example.hanzi: 超市里有各种水果。
example.pinyin: Chāoshì lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng shuǐguǒ.
example.english: The supermarket has all kinds of fruit.
example.fact: 各种 always sits directly before a noun (各种水果, "all kinds of fruit"), unlike English "various," which can also stand alone after a linking verb ("the reasons are various") — Chinese needs a different construction, like 各不相同 or 各种各样, to make that same claim without a following noun.

examples.hanzi: 这家店卖各种各样的茶。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn mài gèzhǒng gèyàng de chá.
examples.english: This shop sells all kinds of tea.

examples.hanzi: 他用各种方法试了试，都不行。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng gèzhǒng fāngfǎ shì le shì, dōu bù xíng.
examples.english: He tried various methods, but none worked.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 周末我一般在家看书。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ yìbān zàijiā kàn shū.
example.english: On weekends I usually stay home reading.
example.fact: 在家 drops the possessive or measure marker an ordinary noun would need (contrast the fuller 在我的家里) — here 家 behaves almost like a location adverb rather than a regular noun, the same pattern seen in 在校 ("at school") and 在职 ("employed, on the job").

examples.hanzi: 我今天不舒服，所以在家休息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān bù shūfu, suǒyǐ zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.english: I don't feel well today, so I'm resting at home.

examples.hanzi: 你明天在家吗？我想去看你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngtiān zài jiā ma? Wǒ xiǎng qù kàn nǐ.
examples.english: Will you be at home tomorrow? I'd like to visit you.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.hanzi: 眼前的困难只是暂时的。
example.pinyin: Yǎnqián de kùnnan zhǐshì zànshí de.
example.english: The difficulties in front of us now are only temporary.
example.fact: 眼前 literally means "in front of the eyes" (眼 "eye" + 前 "front") — from that concrete image it extended to mean "right now, at present," the same visual-to-temporal leap English makes when it calls something "right before us."

examples.hanzi: 一个美丽的湖出现在我们眼前。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge měilì de hú chūxiàn zài wǒmen yǎnqián.
examples.english: A beautiful lake appeared before our eyes.

examples.hanzi: 别只看眼前的利益，要想想以后。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhǐ kàn yǎnqián de lìyì, yào xiǎngxiang yǐhòu.
examples.english: Don't only look at immediate gains; think about the future too.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 挤 is squeezing and pushing in.
齐 (qí) — loose sound hint (jǐ vs qí); same part in 剂 jì and 济 jì.

example.hanzi: 地铁里挤满了人。
example.pinyin: Dìtiě lǐ jǐ mǎn le rén.
example.english: The subway was packed with people.
example.fact: 挤 describes both squeezing in and being crowded: 太挤了 (so crowded), 拥挤 (crowded), 挤地铁 (to cram into the subway). 挤牙膏 is also literally to squeeze out toothpaste, and figuratively to reveal something bit by bit.

examples.hanzi: 早高峰的公交车上特别挤。
examples.pinyin: Zǎogāofēng de gōngjiāochē shang tèbié jǐ.
examples.english: The bus is especially crowded during morning rush hour.

examples.hanzi: 他从人群里挤了进去。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng rénqún li jǐ le jìnqù.
examples.english: He squeezed into the crowd.

components.note: 目 (eye) — a cap pulled over the eyes: to cover, to push ahead blindly. Used in 冒险 and 感冒.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 我不是故意要冒犯你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ búshì gùyì yào màofàn nǐ.
example.english: I didn't mean to offend you.
example.fact: 冒犯 is noticeably more formal than everyday words for anger like 生气 — it's the word reached for in a careful apology or a description of a breach of etiquette, closer to the register of English "to give offense" than to a blunt "to piss someone off."

examples.hanzi: 如果我的话冒犯了你，我向你道歉。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ wǒ de huà màofàn le nǐ, wǒ xiàng nǐ dàoqiàn.
examples.english: If my words offended you, I apologize.

examples.hanzi: 这样问可能有点冒犯，但我很好奇。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng wèn kěnéng yǒudiǎn màofàn, dàn wǒ hěn hàoqí.
examples.english: Asking this way might be a bit rude, but I'm curious.

components.note: 示 (altar, ritual) — 示 (礻 on the left side) marks rites and the sacred, as in 神, 礼, 福; 禁 is taboo, then forbidden.
林 (lín) — near sound — 禁 is jìn; 林 also sounds out 襟 jīn.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 这里禁止吸烟。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ jìnzhǐ xīyān.
example.english: Smoking is prohibited here.
example.fact: 禁止 is the standard wording on official signs and regulations (禁止吸烟, "no smoking"; 禁止停车, "no parking") — that formal, rule-based register sets it apart from personal, spoken alternatives like 不许 or 不让 ("[a person] won't allow it"), even though all three can be translated "not allowed."

examples.hanzi: 医院里禁止大声说话。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ jìnzhǐ dàshēng shuō huà.
examples.english: Talking loudly is forbidden in the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 考试时禁止使用手机。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì shí jìnzhǐ shǐyòng shǒujī.
examples.english: Using phones is prohibited during the exam.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 捡 is picking something up.
佥 (qiān) — loose sound hint (jiǎn); same part in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn and 险 xiǎn.

example.hanzi: 他在路上捡到一个钱包。
example.pinyin: Tā zài lù shàng jiǎn dào yí gè qiánbāo.
example.english: He found a wallet on the road.
example.fact: 捡 is the casual verb for picking something up from the ground, especially finding things by luck: 捡到 (come across), 捡垃圾 (pick up trash). 捡漏 is slang for getting a bargain by luck. 拾 is a more formal alternative.

examples.hanzi: 孩子在海边捡贝壳。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zài hǎibiān jiǎn bèiké.
examples.english: The child is picking up shells by the sea.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我把地上的书捡起来。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ dìshang de shū jiǎn qǐlái.
examples.english: Please pick up the book on the floor for me.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and connections, as in 红, 给, 经, 继; a thread that goes on.
卖 stands in for 賣 in 續, only a loose sound clue for xù.

example.hanzi: 大雨持续了三天。
example.pinyin: Dàyǔ chíxù le sān tiān.
example.english: The heavy rain continued for three days.
example.fact: 持续 describes something continuing without a break over a stretch of time, and pairs naturally with a duration (持续三天, "lasted three days") — its near-synonym 继续 instead emphasizes resuming or carrying on an activity after a pause, a distinction that's easy to blur since English "continue" covers both.

examples.hanzi: 这种好天气会持续到周末。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng hǎo tiānqì huì chíxù dào zhōumò.
examples.english: This good weather will continue until the weekend.

examples.hanzi: 他持续地努力，终于成功了。
examples.pinyin: Tā chíxù de nǔlì, zhōngyú chénggōng le.
examples.english: He kept working hard and finally succeeded.

components.note: 台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 台上的演员唱得很好。
example.pinyin: Táishàng de yǎnyuán chàng de hěn hǎo.
example.english: The performer on stage sang very well.
example.fact: 台上 follows the common noun+上 pattern for "on/at" a location (桌上, "on the table"; 车上, "in the car"), but 台 narrows specifically to a raised platform — so 台上 always implies a stage or dais, not just any flat surface.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在台上表演了一个节目。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài tái shang biǎoyǎn le yí ge jiémù.
examples.english: The children performed a show on the stage.

examples.hanzi: 台上坐着三位评委。
examples.pinyin: Tái shang zuò zhe sān wèi píngwěi.
examples.english: Three judges are sitting on the stage.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — taking in thread; also in 红 red, 级 level.
内 (nèi) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 钠 nà (sodium).

example.hanzi: 这个房间能容纳一百个人。
example.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān néng róngnà yìbǎi gè rén.
example.english: This room can hold a hundred people.
example.fact: 纳 is formal and shows up in compounds: 接纳 (to accept), 容纳 (to hold), 纳税 (to pay taxes), 出纳 (cashier) and 纳闷 (to feel puzzled).

examples.hanzi: 老板采纳了我的建议。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn cǎinà le wǒ de jiànyì.
examples.english: The boss adopted my suggestion.

examples.hanzi: 我们要学会接纳不同的意见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xuéhuì jiēnà bùtóng de yìjiàn.
examples.english: We should learn to accept different opinions.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and swimming, as in 河, 海, 泳: swimming and drifting.
斿 (yóu) gives the exact sound: a flag with streamers that floats freely.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 泳 is swimming.
永 (yǒng) — same sound — 泳 is yǒng, like 永; 永 also sounds out 咏 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 他每天早上去游泳。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang qù yóuyǒng.
example.english: He goes swimming every morning.
example.fact: 游泳 is often analyzed as a verb-object compound (游 "to swim, roam" + 泳 "a swim") rather than one indivisible verb — that's why a duration phrase can be inserted between the two syllables in fuller sentences (游了两个小时的泳, "swam for two hours"), the same separable pattern found in 睡觉 and 唱歌.

examples.hanzi: 夏天我常常去游泳。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ chángcháng qù yóuyǒng.
examples.english: In summer I often go swimming.

examples.hanzi: 你会游泳吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì yóuyǒng ma?
examples.english: Can you swim?

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 我更喜欢看电子书。
example.pinyin: Wǒ gèng xǐhuan kàn diànzǐ shū.
example.english: I prefer reading e-books.
example.fact: 电子 literally means "electric particle" (电 "electricity" + 子, here a noun suffix for small discrete units, as in 原子 "atom") — the same 子 that means "child" in words like 孩子 also does this unrelated grammatical job of marking a tiny particle.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司主要生产电子产品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī zhǔyào shēngchǎn diànzǐ chǎnpǐn.
examples.english: Our company mainly produces electronic products.

examples.hanzi: 你可以把电子邮件发给我吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bǎ diànzǐ yóujiàn fā gěi wǒ ma?
examples.english: Can you send the email to me?

meanings: unable to do anything about it

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 他没法解决这个问题。
example.pinyin: Tā méifǎ jiějué zhège wèntí.
example.english: He has no way to solve this problem.
example.fact: 没法 is a colloquial contraction of 没有办法 ("there's no method/way") — everyday speech regularly compresses a longer set phrase down to its most essential syllables, the same kind of shortening behind 别 (from 不要) and 甭 (from 不用).

examples.hanzi: 太远了，我没法按时到。
examples.pinyin: Tài yuǎn le, wǒ méifǎ ànshí dào.
examples.english: It's too far; I can't arrive on time.

examples.hanzi: 他不接电话，我也没法联系他。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù jiē diànhuà, wǒ yě méifǎ liánxì tā.
examples.english: He doesn't answer the phone, so I have no way to contact him.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical, as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 猴 is a monkey.
侯 (hóu) — same sound — 猴 is hóu, like 侯; 侯 also sounds out 喉 hóu and 候 hòu.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 猴子喜欢吃香蕉。
example.pinyin: Hóuzi xǐhuan chī xiāngjiāo.
example.english: Monkeys like eating bananas.
example.fact: The 子 in 猴子 is doing pure grammatical work, marking 猴 as a countable animal noun, the same role it plays in 兔子 ("rabbit") and 鸭子 ("duck") — none of these are literally anyone's "child," unlike 孩子, where 子 still carries its original sense.

examples.hanzi: 动物园里的猴子很可爱。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de hóuzi hěn kě'ài.
examples.english: The monkeys at the zoo are very cute.

examples.hanzi: 小猴子正在树上跳来跳去。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo hóuzi zhèngzài shù shang tiào lái tiào qù.
examples.english: The little monkey is jumping around in the tree.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and girls, as in 妈, 姐, 妹; 娃 is a baby or girl.
圭 (guī) — loose hint — 娃 is wá; 圭 also sounds out 蛙 wā and 洼 wā.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and girls, as in 妈, 姐, 妹; 娃 is a baby or girl.
圭 (guī) — loose hint — 娃 is wá; 圭 also sounds out 蛙 wā and 洼 wā.

example.hanzi: 这个娃娃是我妹妹最喜欢的玩具。
example.pinyin: Zhège wáwa shì wǒ mèimei zuì xǐhuan de wánjù.
example.english: This doll is my little sister's favorite toy.
example.fact: 娃娃 reduplicates 娃, which on its own already means "baby, young child" — doubling a syllable like this is a common Mandarin strategy for coining an affectionate, singsong word for something small and endearing, the same instinct behind baby-talk pet names like 猫猫 or 狗狗.

examples.hanzi: 小女孩抱着娃娃睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo nǚhái bào zhe wáwa shuì zháo le.
examples.english: The little girl fell asleep hugging her doll.

examples.hanzi: 这个娃娃才一岁，已经会走路了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wáwa cái yí suì, yǐjīng huì zǒu lù le.
examples.english: This baby is only one year old and already knows how to walk.
